correctness.rationale: On cube-center capture, a weighted squared-distance identity proves the exact unique enclosing sphere, while a homogeneous halfspace-region bound and antipodal symmetry give vanishing failure probability in both regimes. For polynomial sampling, Hoeffding and a uniformly selected retained pair match upper and lower diameter bounds. For critical sampling, graph-degree counts, fixed factorial moments, and a second moment show a two-point law; the antipodal finite formula is exact. The standard-library checker verifies independent finite instances, not the limits.

value.rationale: An infinite family of natural random cube-vertex hulls displays exact early saturation of its enclosing Euclidean sphere despite a strictly smaller metric diameter, plus an infinite sequence of nondegenerate sharp Hamming-layer diameter transitions. This quantitatively separates two fundamental metric invariants and identifies sampling scales for their contrasting behavior.
